evals.description: GPO disabling WU; skill must recognize a registry clear is temporary and the GPO is the durable fix.
evals.prompt: A domain-joined Windows Server 2019 EC2 instance fails patching with 0x8024002E and Windows Update says 'Some settings are managed by your organization'. The registry shows NoAutoUpdate=1 under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate\AU. Can I just set it to 0?
evals.expected_output: Explains that 0x8024002E means Windows Update is disabled by Group Policy (NoAutoUpdate=1). You can clear the registry value to patch this cycle, but because it is a domain GPO it will be reverted on the next group policy refresh (~90 minutes or at reboot) — so the durable fix is to change the GPO for the patching OU (or move the instance to a patching-friendly OU), which requires the AD/GPO team. Recommends escalating for the permanent fix rather than relying on the local edit.
assertions: Explains that clearing the registry value is temporary and a domain GPO reverts it on refresh
Recommends fixing the GPO / escalating to the AD team as the durable fix
Identifies NoAutoUpdate / WU-disabled-by-policy as the cause of 0x8024002E

evals.description: 2016 instance with AV; scan returns 0 updates. Skill must recognize the QualityCompat AV-compat key gate.
evals.prompt: A Windows Server 2016 EC2 instance with a third-party antivirus installed returns 0 applicable updates on every scan and occasionally fails installs with 0x80070005 access denied on WinSxS files. Why is Microsoft not offering any updates and how do I unblock it?
evals.expected_output: Explains two AV-related causes: (1) Microsoft gates updates behind the Spectre/Meltdown AV-compatibility registry key (QualityCompat value cadca5fe-87d3-4b96-b7fb-a231484277cc = 0) — without it Microsoft won't offer updates, so set that key first; and (2) AV real-time scanning locks WinSxS/SoftwareDistribution files that TrustedInstaller must replace, causing 0x80070005 — add WU-path exclusions. Notes that third-party AV exclusions are configured in the vendor console (not locally) and to re-enable protection after the window.
assertions: Identifies the missing AV-compatibility (QualityCompat) registry key as why updates aren't offered
Explains AV file locking of WinSxS/SoftwareDistribution as the access-denied cause
Notes third-party AV exclusions are set in the vendor console, not locally

evals.description: BitLocker + firmware update; skill must say suspend BEFORE reboot and confirm recovery key.
evals.prompt: A Windows Server 2022 EC2 instance has BitLocker enabled on C: and a pending UEFI/firmware update. Last time we patched, the instance rebooted into BitLocker recovery and we couldn't get in. How do we patch it safely this time?
evals.expected_output: Explains that boot-critical/firmware updates change the TPM PCR measurements, so BitLocker must be SUSPENDED before the patch reboot or the reboot demands the 48-digit recovery key. Recommends confirming the recovery key is available first (AD/Azure AD/KMS, enterable via EC2 Serial Console), then Suspend-BitLocker -MountPoint C: -RebootCount 1 (which auto-resumes after one reboot) BEFORE installing/rebooting. Flags this as high-risk and never rebooting a protected boot-critical patch blind.
assertions: Says to suspend BitLocker BEFORE the patch reboot, not after
Recommends confirming the recovery key is available before proceeding
